clue.text: Copy a friend who's got it

parts.note: a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the friend is said to have got the word it, so it sits inside the friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to copy a pal who already understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' as the numeral one is a standard crossword convention; 'who's got it' reads as understanding but signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to reproduce or mimic, a straightforward synonym of copying.

clue.text: In the interim, pedestrians create delay

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, people on foot are holding up traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the answer is inside 'interim, pedestrians'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to obstruct or hinder progress, causing delay.

clue.text: At home with 9 and middling host, getting ready to butt in

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: getting something ready involves arranging it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the answer to 9 across

indicators.note: only the central part of the word host is taken

explanation.surface: A man at home with a so-so party host is preparing to interrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ready' signals rearrangement of the 9-across answer with the middle of host; 'At home' as IN is a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to insert oneself or a remark between others, to interrupt or butt in.

clue.text: At first, Adam didn't realise "explain" meant getting to the point

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Adam failed to grasp that a word meant something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' takes the initials of Adam, didn't, realise, explain, meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means relevant to the matter in hand, getting to the point.

clue.text: Deregulation process entails lifting lid on company

indicators.note: processing something works it over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: these letters are lifted out of the pool

explanation.surface: Freeing a firm from rules means taking the top off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' removes the letters of LID from DEREGULATION; 'process' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of attendants or followers, someone's company.

clue.text: Stop official before bad weather

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a sports official
rain is the classic example of bad weather

explanation.surface: A match official calls a halt before a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back or desist, a verb synonym of stop.

clue.text: Swimmer to train with a different foundation

indicators.note: the word's starting letter, its base, is swapped for another

parts.note: to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A swimmer is told to train with a changed groundwork.
explanation.walkthrough: COACH has its first letter changed to R; 'foundation' in a down clue more often means the last letter, so this is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a common freshwater fish, and a fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: A different ratio is applied to deliver certain broadcasts

indicators.note: the anagram goes on after the word for deliver

parts.note: to deliver is to free or set at liberty

indicators.note: a different form of the word means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Applying another ratio is said to produce particular transmissions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges RATIO into TOAIR, which 'is applied to' FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-to-air describes television or radio transmissions available without subscription, a kind of broadcast.

clue.text: Space in hospital department where joiner was is wide open

indicators.note: the word for space goes within the department's letters
the ampersand, a joining word, is replaced, sitting between A and E

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, is a hospital department
a gap is a space

explanation.surface: There is a gap in A and E where a carpenter used to work.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department; GAP replaces its '&'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape means with the mouth wide open in wonder.

clue.text: Simple viewer?

parts.note: unaided sight, the plainest instrument for looking, with no lens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple viewer' suggests a basic gadget; it is unassisted vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing something with the bare organ of sight, without a telescope, is using the plainest viewer.

clue.text: He will fade away when he's out!

definitions.meaning: a man, standing for any male name

definitions.text: will fade away when he's out!
definitions.meaning: joined to out, the name forms an idiom meaning dwindle gradually

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man fainting; 'peter out' means gradually to fade.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb 'peter out' means to diminish gradually and stop, so the man's name joins 'out' to mean fade away.

clue.text: Proprietary name for business brand

parts.note: trade is commerce or business
a mark is a brand or stamp put on goods

explanation.surface: Looking for a word for a company's registered brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a legally registered name or symbol, owned by a firm, identifying its goods.

clue.text: Had trout and a little mackerel served up in port

indicators.note: food served up is dished out in a new arrangement, so these letters are reworked
just a small bit of the fish, its opening letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A diner enjoyed trout with a morsel of mackerel at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes M from mackerel; 'served up' rearranges HADTROUT plus M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmouth is a port town in Devon, south-west England, home of the Royal Navy's officer college.

clue.text: Direction needed to reach initial conclusion

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words before it are wanted

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Advice on which way to go to arrive at a first decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' looks like it qualifies 'conclusion', but it picks the first letters of 'to reach'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general course or tendency, the direction in which things are moving.

clue.text: Alienated Tom by assuming a defensive position

indicators.note: the letters take on a new shape, assuming another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An estranged Tom has taken up a guarded stance.
explanation.walkthrough: A motte and bailey is a Norman castle: a keep on a mound (motte) above a walled courtyard (bailey).
explanation.definitionFit: The Norman fortification of earthwork mound plus enclosure was built as a strongpoint, a defensive position.

clue.text: Signature tune of a narcissist?

parts.note: a self-obsessed person's anthem would be a song all about himself, split as ...

explanation.walkthrough: A signature tune is an identifying melody; split differently, it is the song about me.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature tune identifies a show or performer, and split up it is a self-lover's song.

clue.text: Determined unbeliever has lost his affliction and gone outside!

indicators.note: the word for gone surrounds the shortened unbeliever

parts.note: died means gone, passed away

indicators.note: the unbeliever drops part of himself

parts.note: an agnostic doubts God's existence
a tic is a twitching affliction

explanation.surface: A sceptic who shed his twitch has stepped out with his mind made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' and 'outside' look like part of the story about a sceptic; 'Determined' is the definition, in its sense of diagnosed or established.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's diagnosis determines a condition, so diagnosed means identified or determined.

clue.text: Restrict the French Society no end

parts.note: to limit is to restrict
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: Curbing French society would be endless work.
explanation.definitionFit: Limitless means boundless, having no end.

clue.text: Provide actor with cue that's faulty

indicators.note: a faulty arrangement is a wrong one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer is given a mistaken prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges ACTOR and CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to equip or provide with dress and gear.

clue.text: The choicest French dessert cleared up by yours truly!

parts.note: creme, as in creme caramel or creme brulee, is a French dessert

indicators.note: something stirred up is mixed, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: yours truly is the setter referring to himself, giving me

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having polished off the finest French pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals rearranging the word cleared; 'yours truly' is the setter speaking of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally cream of the cream, means the very best of a group, the choicest.

clue.text: A 10-0 reverse will get the bird

indicators.note: a reverse is a defeat, but here it turns the score backwards

parts.note: ten nil is a score of 10-0

explanation.surface: A heavy 10-0 defeat means the team gets jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' is a defeat in the surface; 'get the bird' means be booed.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch, a songbird.

clue.text: As a snooker player might be at the right moment

definitions.text: As a snooker player might be
definitions.meaning: a snooker player leans over and rests on the stick used to strike balls
exactly when expected, like an actor coming in on the prompt

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely on time, and literally a snooker player can be resting on the cue.

clue.text: Many are suffering for the Treasury

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: Lots of people are hurting because of the Finance Ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of valuables, a treasury.

clue.text: The last edition tenor corrected for composer

indicators.note: something corrected is put right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: The final printing of a tenor's score has been amended for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges Z, EDITION and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was an Italian composer of bel canto operas such as Lucia di Lammermoor.

clue.text: Motivate to go by car

definitions.meaning: to travel in a motor vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to propel someone to act, and also to travel by car.

clue.text: Nothing in US at university to stimulate

parts.note: zip is American slang for nothing
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Having nothing at an American college is a spur.
explanation.definitionFit: To zip up something is to enliven or invigorate it, stimulate.

clue.text: Private eyes get encouragement in the scientific study of buildings

indicators.note: the word for encouragement is placed in the word for private eyes

parts.note: a tec, short for detective, is a private eye; tecs is the plural
a tonic is something that gives a lift, encouragement

explanation.surface: Detectives receive a boost while investigating architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Tectonics usually means the study of the earth's crust, but it also means the art or science of building construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides geology, the word denotes the science or art of construction, the study of buildings.

clue.text: Groom to give himself a pat on the back

definitions.meaning: to tidy one's appearance, as a bird does its feathers

definitions.text: to give himself a pat on the back
definitions.meaning: to congratulate oneself, take self-satisfied pride

explanation.definitionFit: To preen is both to tidy oneself with care and to congratulate oneself smugly.

clue.text: 25, for example, arranged table decoration

indicators.note: something arranged is put into order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across

explanation.surface: An instance of preening is set out as a centrepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles PREEN plus EG.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, often with dishes or holders.

clue.text: Lay down payment

definitions.meaning: to put something down or set it in place
a sum paid in advance as security

explanation.definitionFit: To deposit is to set down; a deposit is also a part payment made up front.
